items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I remembered Joe Carroll in Toledo was singing with Dizzy, which was my gig, I was supposed to be Dizzy’s first singer... So I called Joe and I said, “where is Bird?”

ctx.x: So finally I said that’s enough, you’d better stop, so I quit. And Kenny Dorham got up from his chair next to Bird and he was starting to play his solo, and I started to leave the bandstand. And I felt this tug on my coattail. I’m trying to leave, and this — and I look and there’s Bird and he’s got ahold of my coattail, and so I turned back. You know I’ve been in show business all my life so I made it look like I’d just changed my mind, because of the audience. So I turned back and he says to sit in the chair…

that is not done. But I never paid any attention to those things. I truly never paid attention to any of that stuff. So here I was in this situation where they had sent a guy to my house and he told me he says, “Jon, you’ve got to withdraw your name.” I said, “why? I earned it, are you kidding? I earned that.” He says, “look, if you insist on this, they’re going to lean on me, and you know I’ve got a wife and two kids.” I said, “okay.” So I said hum, that means I’m not going anywhere in Toledo, however brilliant…

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I called Joe Carroll... But I liked Joe. He was a beautiful guy. So I called him up.

ctx.x: They – the police, or the border guard.

The border people. When they found out I wanted to live in Canada – I wanted to move to Canada. See, if I hadn’t said I wanted to move, I could have come in and just stayed there, but I was a straight-laced law-student person, and I just told them what I had in mind, which was disastrous, because I couldn’t do it for under – without $1,000. So there I was, outside Buffalo. What to do? What to do? I had an old Buick, which was rattling by that time. Then my wife and my son, and my drums in the trunk. So I thought,…

What does it cost?” He said, “$16 a week you can get a room there.” I said, “Great. Where’s Bird?” He said, “Bird is at the Apollo Bar, 125th Street and Seventh Avenue.” This is two years and four months. I just started laughing like a crazy man. I just cracked up, because there he was, like he said. Just ask anybody. So I really – I just laughed for about a half…
